summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with symptoms of urinary tract infection following a nephrostomy tube and stent replacement, including low-grade fever, chills, nausea, and flank pain. She was started on linezolid for presumed infection, and urine cultures later confirmed E. coli, leading to a switch to oral cefpodoxime. Leakage around the tube persisted, prompting a second tube replacement, after which drainage improved and symptoms resolved. Her kidney function stabilized with creatinine returning to baseline. A psychiatry consult addressed her emotional distress related to recurrent hospitalizations and family stress, and she was transitioned from atovaquone to dapsone due to nausea. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor nephrostomy output, continue antibiotics, and follow up with the transplant and mental health teams.
